2026-12-10.title: Thursday of the Second Week of Advent
readings: I, the Lord your God, hold your right hand
The Lord is gracious and merciful; slow to anger, and of great kindness
No one greater than John the Baptist has arisen
2026-12-10.alt: Optional memorial: Our Lady of Loreto.
2026-12-10.verse: Truly I tell you, among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
theo: “For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand; it is I who say to you, ‘Do not fear, I will help you.’” Isaiah calls Israel a “worm”, small and weak, yet God will make it a threshing sledge. For the poor and thirsty he opens rivers on bare heights and turns the desert into pools, “so that all may see and know… that the hand of the LORD has done this.”

Jesus praises John the Baptist: no one born of women is greater. Yet “the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he”. John stands at the threshold; the disciples of Jesus enter the Kingdom through Baptism and become children of God. Greatness in the Kingdom is not our achievement but God's gift, received by the little ones who let God take their hand.
outline: Ask: when did you last feel God holding your hand?
Point 1 · I hold your right hand
God's personal care for the weak.
Point 3 · The least in the Kingdom
Baptism gives us a greatness beyond John's.
“Do not fear, I will help you.”
live: When afraid today, open your right hand in prayer and say: “Lord, hold me.”
Find out your baptism date and celebrate it.
2026-12-10.prayer: Lord my God, you hold my right hand and say, “Do not fear.” Open rivers in the dry places of my life, and make me little enough to enter your Kingdom. Amen.
altar: At Mass we receive what the prophets longed to see: Christ himself. The least in the Kingdom is fed with the Bread of Life.

quick: He opens rivers in the desert for the thirsty.
The least in the Kingdom is greater than John.
2026-12-10.action: Find and celebrate your baptism date.
2026-12-10.question: Do I let God hold my hand?

family.explain: God says: do not be afraid, I will help you. Even when we feel small, God holds our hand.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we feel small, and how does God help us?”

pm.open: Lord God, you hold us by the right hand and say: do not fear, I will help you. As we gather, turn our dryness into springs of living water. Amen.
share: God says: do not fear, I will help you (Isaiah 41:13). Where do I feel small and afraid?
Jesus says the least in the Kingdom is greater than John (Matthew 11:11). What great gifts have I received?
What dry place in my life needs God's water?
pm.resp: The Lord is our helper; we shall not fear.
interc: For the Church, that she may be grateful for the riches of the Kingdom.
For those who feel small and afraid, that God may hold their hand.
For regions suffering drought and water shortage.
For prophets and witnesses of truth in our time.
For our group, that we may use our gifts generously.
pm.close: Lord God, Holy One of Israel, you help the weak and make the desert bloom. Hold us by the hand, and make us fruitful with the gifts of your Kingdom. Amen.

illus: A small girl in a Kerala parish was asked why she gave her birthday money to the Advent collection for the poor. She said: “Jesus gave me everything. I'm only little, but I can give a little.”

homily: Dear friends, God speaks through Isaiah with great tenderness: do not fear, you worm Jacob, you insect Israel! I will help you, says the Lord; your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel (Isaiah 41:14). God calls his people a worm, not to insult them but to show how small and weak they feel, and how strong he is for them.
He promises: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water (Isaiah 41:18). God turns dryness into life.
In the Gospel Jesus praises John the Baptist: among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist. Yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he (Matthew 11:11).

How can the least be greater than John? Not because we are holier than John, but because we live after the coming of Christ. We have received what John only announced: the death and resurrection of Jesus, baptism, the Holy Spirit, the Eucharist. We are given more than the greatest prophet.

This should give us both gratitude and responsibility. If we have received so much, how much more should we bear fruit? John lived in the desert on locusts and wild honey and gave his life for the truth. What do we give?

When you feel small, remember: God says, do not fear, I will help you. And when you feel proud, remember: all you have is gift. Let us thank God today for the riches of the Kingdom, and use them generously this Advent. Amen.
kids: Children, God holds your hand like a loving father. You never walk alone!

intro: Theme: “Do not fear, I will help you.”
God holds our hand, opens rivers in the desert, and makes the least great in his Kingdom.

q: For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand; it is I who say to you, “Do not fear, I will help you.”
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Pray “Lord, hold me” when afraid today.

sub: God opens rivers on bare heights.
All will know his hand did it.
q: When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue is parched with thirst, I the LORD will answer them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them. I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink. As the scripture has said, “Out of the believer's heart shall flow rivers of living water.”
points.apply: Bring a dry area of your life to Jesus.

sub: John is the greatest of the prophets.
Baptism makes us children of the Kingdom.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Truly I tell you, among those born of women no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

concl: God holds us by the hand.
Little ones are great in his Kingdom.
2026-12-10.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises before Christmas.
